title: Reciprocal rank fusion
text: Reciprocal rank fusion combines several ranked lists by summing one over k plus the rank of each document, which needs no score calibration between systems.

title: Okapi BM25
text: BM25 is a lexical ranking function based on term frequency saturation and document length normalisation, and it remains a strong baseline for keyword queries.

title: Dense bi-encoder retrieval
text: A bi-encoder maps queries and passages into the same vector space so that semantically similar text has a high cosine similarity even with no shared words.

title: Cross-encoder reranking
text: A cross-encoder reads the query and the passage together in one transformer forward pass, which is far more accurate than a bi-encoder but far too slow to score a whole corpus.

title: Normalised discounted cumulative gain
text: nDCG rewards placing highly relevant documents near the top of the ranking by discounting gains logarithmically with rank and dividing by the ideal ordering.

title: Inverted index
text: An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents that contain it, which is what makes lexical search fast over millions of documents.

title: Approximate nearest neighbour search
text: FAISS inverted file and product quantisation indexes trade a little recall for large reductions in query latency and memory footprint.

title: Vocabulary mismatch
text: Lexical retrieval fails when the query and the relevant document use different words for the same concept, which is the gap dense retrieval was designed to close.

title: Mean reciprocal rank
text: MRR averages one over the rank of the first relevant result, so it measures how quickly a user reaches a single correct answer.

title: Chunking long documents
text: Splitting long documents into overlapping passages keeps each embedding focused on one topic at the cost of a larger index.

title: Query latency budgets
text: Interactive search is usually held to a p95 latency budget in the low hundreds of milliseconds, which rules out rescoring deep candidate lists with a large model.

title: Exact match search for identifiers
text: When a user searches for a product code, an error string or a rare proper noun, exact lexical matching beats semantic similarity because the token itself is the intent.
